content.text:
Yes, H3 explains the data: two planets with free eccentricities bring the scatter under the limit, and nothing significant is left in the residuals.

**Best fit: F7** (H3, period tolerance widened to 0.25). The first fit, F5 at the default 0.1 tolerance, had planet 1 stuck on its search bound at 16.797 d. The refit F7 converged with **no flags**.

| | Period | Amplitude K | Eccentricity | ω |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Planet 1 | 16.865 d (started at 15.27 d) | 41.79 m/s | 0.108 | 2.83 rad |
| Planet 2 | 11.340 d (started at 10.40 d) | 23.12 m/s | 0.093 | 5.91 rad |

- **Scatter (RMS):** 3.55 m/s, limit 4.37 m/s, so it passes. Reduced χ² is 1.80 (1 would be a perfect match to the measurement errors).
- **BIC:** 389.4, lower is better.
  - That is 6195.9 below the no-planet model, 949 below the 1-planet fit F1 (1690.8), and 949 below the 15.15 d + 1.74 d fit F2 (1338.6). A difference of 10 or more is decisive.
  - It is the same as F4, the fit of H5 (389.41). H3 and H5 end at the same solution, so they are effectively one hypothesis.
- **Residual periodogram of F7:** no peak reaches the 1% false-alarm threshold.

| Residual peak | False-alarm probability |
|---|---|
| 2.82 d (strongest) | 5.9% |
| 2.55 d | 9.7% |
| 1.45 d | 22% |
| 1.39 d | 53% |
| 2.28 d | 55% |
| 1.13 d | 83% |

The 1.45 d and 1.39 d peaks are tied to 2.82 d as harmonics, so they are not separate features. The 1.13 d and 2.28 d peaks are tied to each other the same way. The tool found no sampling aliases.

**Caveats:**
- Both periods ended about 10% above their starting values (15.27 → 16.87 d and 10.40 → 11.34 d). The best periods therefore sit well away from the residual periodogram peaks the hypothesis came from.
- The data span only 37.25 d, which is about 2.2 cycles of the outer planet. The exact periods are therefore only loosely pinned down, even though the fit is good.
- The 2.82 d peak (5.9%) is the only lead worth watching. It is not significant, and I did not add a planet for it.

H3 explains the data: two mildly eccentric planets near 16.9 d and 11.3 d fit within the scatter limit and leave no significant residual signal.
